agentEditor.descriptionNew: A name, a role, standing instructions — and what it may use.
agentEditor.lockedHint: Set by people who can manage workspace settings.
agentEditor.handleHint: Written as @handle in transcripts and chat.
agentEditor.roleHint: One line. Shown next to the name and injected into the prompt.
agentEditor.whenToUseHint: One sentence. Shown in the @-menu and on the card, so a person can pick the right agent without reading the prompt.
agentEditor.whenToUsePlaceholder: Guards margin and cash; asks what a decision costs.
agentEditor.instructionsHint: How this agent behaves everywhere it appears. Be specific about what it owns and what it should refuse to answer.
agentEditor.answerStyleHint: Applied under the instructions in chat.
agentEditor.modelRouteHint: Which configured route serves this agent's turns.
agentEditor.temperatureHint: 0 is deterministic, 2 is wild. Blank uses the model's default.
agentEditor.turnCapHint: Characters per turn in meetings. Blank means no cap.
agentEditor.toolsAll: Every tool, including ones added later. Untick one to restrict this agent.
agentEditor.toolsSome: {count} of {total} tools. New tools stay off until you add them.
agentEditor.pictureHint: Shown instead of initials in chat, meetings and the roster. Pick one of the shipped works, paste an https link, or leave it blank for initials.
agentEditor.colourHint: Used for the avatar and the transcript.
agentEditor.nodeHint: Leave blank to run in this app process.
agentEditor.ignoredKeys: Ignored keys this format does not know: {keys}
agentEditor.fileLocked: The same agent as a file: front matter for the settings, the body is the instructions. Read-only for you, because a file rewrites the handle, autonomy and tools too; change the instructions on the Definition tab, or export this one.
agentEditor.fileEditable: The same agent as a file: front matter for the settings, the body is the instructions. Paste an agent written for OpenCode or Claude Code here and press Apply; export to carry this one elsewhere.
agentEditor.footerLocked: Handle, autonomy, tools, route and node are set by people who can manage workspace settings.
agentEditor.footerStarter: Starter agent — you can always restore the shipped version.

agentsPane.heading: Agents
agentsPane.rosterCount: {active} on the roster{retired, plural, =0 {} other { · # retired}}
agentsPane.emptyTitleManager: Pick an agent, or write one
agentsPane.emptyBody: An agent is a name, a role and standing instructions grounded in a method that works. The same agent sits in meetings, answers in chat when picked or @mentioned, and can be exported as a file.
agentsPane.retiredNotice: {name} retired. Past transcripts keep the name.
agentsPane.conflictBody: {name} already uses the handle in {file}. Replacing swaps its definition for the file's.
agentsPane.useInChatTitle: Pick this agent in the chat composer
agentsPane.putInMeetingTitle: Open a new meeting with this agent seated
agentsPane.styleBadge: {style, select, concise {concise} detailed {detailed} academic {academic} organized {organized} other {{style}}}
agentsPane.instructionsNote: In chat these instructions go above the answer style{style, select, none {} other { ({style})}}; in a meeting they go under the meeting's objective, agenda and current phase. The agent always sees the workspace's cited passages when retrieval is on.
agentsPane.fileIntro: The same agent as a file — front matter for the settings, the body is the instructions. It is the shape OpenCode and Claude Code agents use, so it moves between tools.
agentsPane.fileIntroImport: Import one with the upload button on the left.
agentsPane.suggestionAsk: What should I ask you about, {name}?
agentsPane.suggestionRisk: Summarize what my sources say about our biggest risk right now.
agentsPane.suggestionPushBack: What would you push back on in our current plan?
agentsPane.tryTitle: Try {name} before you rely on it
agentsPane.tryBody: A scratch conversation held with this agent over the workspace's sources, through the same route the main chat uses. Nothing here is saved.
agentsPane.footer: Enter to send · answers cite the workspace's sources · not saved to your chat history

agentsPanel.retiredNotice: {name} retired. Past transcripts keep their name.
agentsPanel.autonomyDescription: How much an agent may do without a person in the loop. The room's least autonomous agent decides what a meeting may do; the API refuses the rest.
agentsPanel.defaultAssistantDescription: How Launchstack answers in chat when no agent is picked, for everyone who hasn't chosen their own style under Settings › Appearance. Each agent carries its own style, so this is the one place a style is a chat setting rather than an agent setting.
agentsPanel.rosterDescription: The same agents sit in meetings, answer in chat when picked or @mentioned, and can be tried out on the Agents app. Editing one changes what it does next time — never what it said last time.
agentsPanel.tryNote: Try an agent before putting it in a room, or import one from a definition file, in Studio → Agents.
agentsPanel.nodeDisconnected: Node "{node}" is not connected — turns for this agent will fail until it registers
agentsPanel.machinesDescription: An agent can run on a different machine from this app. The worker dials in and answers turn requests — all outbound, so it needs no public address of its own.
agentsPanel.remoteOff: Remote agents are off. Set COLLAB_HUB_SECRET on this deployment to accept worker machines — until then every agent runs in this process.
agentsPanel.nodeNote: Set an agent's node id to that COLLAB_NODE_ID and its turns are produced on that machine, against that machine's model. Each message records the node that served it, so a transcript shows where every turn came from.

meetingsHome.heading: Put your agents in a room and give them a job
meetingsHome.intro: A meeting is a channel where the participants are agents and you are a participant too. Pick a workflow, choose the room, press run. The transcript is the record; the minutes are extracted from it, never invented.

workflow.title: Pick a workflow
workflow.body: A recipe: the objective, the agenda, who belongs in the room, and the phases the conversation moves through.

room.title: Choose the room
room.body: Any of your agents can take a seat. Each speaks from its standing instructions and cites the workspace's sources.

run.title: Run it, step in any time
run.body: Turns run on their own. Read along, add a comment, take the floor, or take over an agent's seat. Minutes are extracted from what was said.

meetingsHome.runningCount: {count, plural, one {# meeting running} other {# meetings running}}
meetingsHome.recentHint: Reopen a room to read the transcript or its minutes.
meetingsHome.workflowsHint: Each card is a method teams already run — named on the card — turned into phases the engine enforces. Everything is editable before you start.
meetingsHome.agentsHint: The same roster answers in chat and sits in meetings. Try one out or write your own.
meetingsHome.noPhases: No phases — the turn policy runs the room.

meetingsPane.empty: No meetings yet. Pick a workflow on the home screen to start one.
meetingsPane.nothingSaid: Nothing said yet. Press Run to let the agents take their turns, or write the first message yourself.
meetingsPane.servedBy: This turn was produced on node "{node}"
meetingsPane.noPhases: No phases — the turn policy runs the whole meeting. Start the next one from a workflow to get diverge / critique / decide stretches.
meetingsPane.minutesStats: {turns, plural, one {# agent turn} other {# agent turns}} · {humans, plural, one {# human message} other {# human messages}}
meetingsPane.minutesNote: Extracted from the transcript, never generated — every line above was said by someone in this channel.
meetingsPane.speakingAs: Speaking as {seat} — the agents are on hold
meetingsPane.haveFloor: You have the floor — the agents are on hold
meetingsPane.addComment: Add a comment. The agents will read it on their next turn.
meetingsPane.pausedNote: Agent turns are paused while you hold the floor.
meetingsPane.hintRunning: Enter to send · your message lands in the transcript before the next agent turn
meetingsPane.hintIdle: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line

roundRobin.label: Round robin
roundRobin.description: Everyone speaks in turn. Predictable, and no one dominates.

moderated.label: Moderated
moderated.description: A chair opens, closes, and hands the floor to whoever they name.

reactive.label: Reactive
reactive.description: Whoever was addressed speaks next; otherwise the closest role picks it up.

newMeeting.description: Pick a workflow, choose who's in the room, and press start. The workflow fills in the rest — change any of it first.
newMeeting.objectiveHint: What the meeting has to produce. Every agent sees it on every turn.
newMeeting.objectivePlaceholder: Agree a Q3 price change and name who ships it
newMeeting.anyAgent: Any agent can take a seat; manage the roster in Studio → Agents.
newMeeting.noAgents: No agents yet — add one in Studio → Agents.
newMeeting.phasesOnHint: The engine keeps each phase to its speakers and goal, and announces the change in the channel.
newMeeting.phasesOffHint: Off — the turn policy runs the whole meeting.
newMeeting.turnLimitBelow: Below the {turns} turns the phases add up to — the meeting will stop before the last phase.
newMeeting.turnLimitHint: A hard stop. The meeting also ends early once the objective is met.
newMeeting.agendaPlaceholder:
Current margin
Proposed change
Owner and timing
newMeeting.slackHint: Turns are posted to this channel, and messages people write there come back here.
newMeeting.mirrorLabel: Mirror the meeting to this channel

errors.notStarter: @{handle} is not a starter agent, so there is no shipped version to restore

errors.fileOutOfRange: The file parsed, but a field is out of range
errors.roomReadOnly: An agent in this room is set to "Read only", so turns only happen when someone presses Step. Raise its autonomy under Workspace › Agents to let the meeting run on its own.

phaseProblems.needsTurnUntitled: Phase {index} needs at least one turn.
phaseProblems.speakersAbsentUntitled: Phase {index} names speakers who are not in the room.
